merger_name: Mitsubishi Electric Corporation – Power Costs, Inc.

anzsic_codes.name: Other Electrical and Electronic Goods Wholesaling
Computer System Design and Related Services

merger_description:
Mitsubishi Electric Corporation (**MELCO**) proposes to indirectly acquire 100% of the equity interests in Power Costs, Inc., (trading as PCI Energy Solutions, Inc.) (**PCI**) from Power Costs HoldCo, Inc. (the **Acquisition**).

MELCO is a Japanese multinational electronics and electrical equipment manufacturing company. MELCO’s global operations comprise a range of automation and processing technologies. MELCO also offers software solutions, which are used for operation, maintenance and control in automation processes.

MELCO’s Australian operations predominantly relate to the supply of air conditioning and refrigeration units, home appliances, factory automation products, automotive parts, power systems, railways, defence-related, and communication systems. It also offers solutions across the education, aged care, data centres, residential living, manufacturing, healthcare and transport/logistics sectors. In respect of solutions in the energy industry, MELCO supplies physical equipment such as energy generators, as well as control systems (i.e., hardware).

PCI is an Oklahoma-based provider of full-spectrum energy software and support for energy enterprises. Its software solutions are used by clients operating in the wholesale market for the supply of power, including public and privately owned power utilities, energy marketers and traders.

In particular, PCI offers software solutions designed to streamline energy trading and managing energy transmission and reliability. In Australia, PCI’s key product offering is an Outage Management System which streamlines communications between plant and operations personnel to manage outages efficiently.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship
between MELCO and PCI in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of both power generation
equipment and control systems for energy markets and
control software for energy markets in Australia.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
